transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, what made me come in is that I've been having some trouble at work. I'm a receptionist, and lately, I've started losing my place while I'm scheduling appointments or, you know, working on the lobby displays. It's like my mind just slips off track because I'm busy thinking about what else I might have overlooked or forgotten to do. It's just getting a bit frustrating.
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty staying on track or forgetfulness since you were a child, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

No, it's definitely a newer problem for me. I never really struggled with this kind of thing when I was younger. It's been going on for about nine months now. It all started right after... well, I had an overnight detention and there was a whole paperwork mix-up around it. Ever since that happened, I've just been having these issues staying focused.
Since that incident nine months ago, do you find yourself having unwanted, vivid memories or nightmares about what happened?

No, I don't really have anything like that. I mean, I think about the mix-up a lot, and it definitely stresses me out, but I don't have nightmares about it or feel like I'm reliving it or anything. It's more just... worrying about making another mistake like that again.
Beyond the worry about your work performance, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or have you lost interest in the activities you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. I mean, I still enjoy doing my usual things outside of work. It's really just the constant worrying that's getting to me, not feeling depressed or anything like that.
Aside from your concerns about work, do you find that you are constantly worried about many other aspects of your life, such as your health, finances, or family?

Yeah, actually, I do. I find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things now, not just my job performance. Um, things like paying bills, travel plans, or just keeping everyday schedules straight. It's like... well, I just constantly worry about little paperwork errors or mistakes, feeling like one small mix-up is somehow going to turn into a much bigger problem.
